messages:
scancode-bot: ALERT: potential secret match in build log for repo `infra-deploy` run #342. Pattern looks like AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID. Link: https://ci.redwood.internal/runs/342 (:warning:)
jamal: 👀 can someone pick this up? I'm in standup for 20m.
alex: I'll take it, pulling the build log now.
alex: snippet from log (redacted):
```
[2026-03-20T10:12:03Z] export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIAxxxxxREDACTED1234
[2026-03-20T10:12:03Z] export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=*****
```
maria: thanks. I searched IAM activity — found a key with last use 2 days ago that matches the pattern (partial match). I'm starting a revoke.
ops-oncall: I've put a temporary deny on that key in IAM and created INC-2026 in PagerDuty. Blocking access from prod accounts for now.
jamal: we should rotate any service accounts that might have used this. Which pipeline used this key?
alex: the key was injected via a GH Actions secret in `infra-deploy` legacy workflow. Looks like a runner step echoed env vars into the build log during a failure case.
emily: running a grep across archived runner logs for the past 90 days now. Also scanning other repos for similar workflows.
security-lead: good containment steps. Don't post externally yet. We need scope: repo-only leak vs. public exposure. Maria, can you confirm whether the leaked key had any S3 or KMS permissions?
maria: key had limited IAM policy: s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject on `redwood-ci-artifacts-prod` and kms:Decrypt on cmk-arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111111111111:key/abcd-1234 (customer-managed). I'm kicking CMK policy review now.
ops-oncall: artifact bucket had object uploads from that run. I removed public-read ACL on the object and tightened bucket policy. Also added a lifecycle rule to quarantine old logs for forensic analysis.
alex: will scrub the runner workflow to stop printing envs; changing `set -x` in scripts and masking variables in GH Actions.
emily: scan progress: 1 repo flagged (this one) with matching build log. 0 matches in repo history so far (running full git history scan with git-secrets + truffleHog). I'll post results in INC-2026.
scancode-bot: NOTE: artifacts in `redwood-ci-artifacts-prod` were encrypted with CMK abcd-1234. If we rotate/disable that key, decrypts will fail for older artifacts. Consider exporting copies if needed.
maria: acknowledging. I'll restrict CMK key policy to only allow decrypt for the infra role and schedule rotation for 24h out. Ops, coordinate artifact access before rotation.
ops-oncall: coordinating. Also updating GH runner to redact env in logs and adding post-run cleanup to remove any temporary credentials.
jamal: can we do retroactive audit of build logs and cached artifacts on runners? We need regex across archived logs and runner cache blobs.
emily: yes, running that now against logs stored in `ci-logs-archive` and runner caches in the S3 runner bucket. Will attach list to the ticket.
security-lead: comms plan: internal only for now. If keys had external access or we find exfiltration, we'll escalate to legal and PR. For customers, wait till we have confirmed scope.
alex: created branch to update workflows: mask secrets, remove `set -x`, add `actions/setup-aws` usage for ephemeral creds. Will open PR and tag @ops-oncall for quick review.
maria: rotated any IAM creds that used that key, created replacements, and rotated tokens in affected services. Logged all rotations in the incident tracker.
ops-oncall: redeploying runners with updated envs and new credentials. Updating deploy pipelines to use KMS-encrypted secrets instead of raw env vars in workflows.
jamal: added observability task: log token revocations as audit events and emit alert if revoked key seen in new logs. Also scheduled a 24h re-scan.
emily: follow-ups: add pre-commit git-secrets hook to infra repos, add a CI check that fails if runner logs contain env var patterns, and prevent uploading raw logs to unencrypted buckets.
security-lead: after containment, we'll run a blameless postmortem. Action items: update workflows, run org-wide leak scan, KMS policy hardening, add CI masking. Owner list assigned in INC-2026.
scancode-bot: SCAN SUMMARY: 1 exposed AWS key detected in build log of `infra-deploy` run #342. No repo history matches (scan complete). Artifacts quarantined and ACLs fixed.
ops-oncall: marking incident as contained pending final confirmation of key revocation and successful redeploys. Will close once operations validate.
jamal: thanks team :thumbsup: if anyone finds more hits ping channel and add to INC-2026.
security-lead: good work, keep updates in the ticket and we'll schedule a 48h check-in to confirm no downstream impacts.
